IMPORTANT_tautology_finding.warning: The 1.0 test macro-F1 above is NOT evidence of a validated, independent bearing-fault detector. rms and kurtosis are BOTH direct inputs to this model AND the exact quantities the labels were derived from (see models/vibration/vibration_task_definition.json). A sufficiently expressive model can trivially reconstruct the labeling rule from those two features alone - this is label leakage via feature identity, not learned physical insight.
IMPORTANT_tautology_finding.ablation_performed: Retrained RandomForest (same split, same seed) with reduced feature sets to check for genuine independent signal:
IMPORTANT_tautology_finding.interpretation: Excluding the exact labeling variables still gives 0.968 F1 because std/crest_factor/peak/peak_to_peak are mechanically correlated proxies for the same amplitude signal. Only when ALL amplitude-related features are removed (leaving just dominant_frequency, spectral_centroid, spectral_bandwidth, skewness) does the score drop to a still-strong-but-honestly-lower 0.857 - this is the best available estimate of genuinely independent discriminative signal in this dataset, and it IS real (well above chance for 3 imbalanced classes), just weaker than the full/tautological number implies.
IMPORTANT_tautology_finding.recommendation: Report 1.0 only alongside this caveat. Treat 0.857 (spectral-only) as the more scientifically honest lower-bound estimate of real generalizable signal. The exported model (using all 10 features) is legitimate as a fast, portable implementation of the derived labeling rule, but must not be marketed as an independently-validated fault classifier.

temporal_behavior_check.method: Predictions from both the full model and a spectral-only (non-tautological) model were generated across the ENTIRE chronological trajectory (all 2156 files, train+val+test) and compared against the derived labels in 150-file chunks.
temporal_behavior_check.finding: Both models show a physically coherent temporal progression: healthy (files ~0-150) -> transition to degrading (~150-300) -> sustained degrading with a gradually increasing fraction of severe predictions from ~file 600 onward -> severe becomes dominant near the end (~file 1950+). This matches the expected bearing-spalling narrative (progressive worsening, not random oscillation). The spectral-only model's agreement with the derived label stays above ~90% through most of the trajectory and only drops near the very end (59% in the final 56-file chunk), which is expected since it cannot see the amplitude signal the label partly depends on.
temporal_behavior_check.verdict: Temporally sensible - not flagged as randomly oscillating.
